sourceLesson.title: Numbers, Time and Measurements
sourceLesson.titleFrench: Les nombres, l'heure et les mesures
sourceLesson.objective: Use numbers, prices in pesos, clock times and café quantities to order and check a total.
sourceLesson.focus: Numbers 0 to 1,000, prices in pesos, clock time, and café quantities like cups and pieces

cardFrench.note: Quelle heure est-il ? means what time is it?
Mexican bakeries count sweet bread by the piece.
In Mexico, une portion de chilaquiles is one plate or serving.

cardFrench.fr: Une table pour 4, s'il vous plaît.
3 pièces de pain sucré mexicain, s'il vous plaît.

cardFrench.note: Always use il est: il est 1 heure for one o'clock, il est 8 heures for eight.

cardFrench.fr: Le petit-déjeuner, c'est de 7 h à 11 h ?

readerFrench.english: Emma walks into Café Luna in the morning.
readerFrench.french: Emma entre au Café Luna le matin.

readerFrench.english: Emma looks at the time: It's half past 8.
readerFrench.french: Emma regarde l'heure : il est 8 heures et demie.

readerFrench.english: Luis: There are servings of chilaquiles until noon.
readerFrench.french: Luis : Il y a des portions de chilaquiles jusqu'à midi.

readerFrench.english: Luis: The cup costs 30 pesos and the glass 35.
readerFrench.french: Luis : La tasse coûte 30 pesos et le verre 35.

readerFrench.english: Emma: In a cup, and 3 pieces of sweet bread.
readerFrench.french: Emma : En tasse, et 3 pièces de pain sucré mexicain.

readerFrench.english: Luis: The piece costs 20 pesos and the dozen 200.
readerFrench.french: Luis : La pièce coûte 20 pesos et la douzaine 200.

readerFrench.english: Luis: Yes, and the slice of cake costs 45.
readerFrench.french: Luis : Oui, et la part de gâteau coûte 45.

forms.sourceLine: Emma mira la hora: Son las 8 y media.
forms.englishPrompt: Emma looks at the time: It's half past 8.
forms.frenchAnswer: Emma regarde l'heure : il est 8 heures et demie.
forms.explanation: Son las 8 y media becomes il est 8 heures et demie. The digit 8 is kept as in the source; French uses il est for every hour and adds heures.

forms.sourceLine: Luis: Hay órdenes de chilaquiles hasta el mediodía.
forms.englishPrompt: Luis: There are servings of chilaquiles until noon.
forms.frenchAnswer: Luis : Il y a des portions de chilaquiles jusqu'à midi.
forms.explanation: Hay órdenes becomes il y a des portions; chilaquiles stays as the Mexican dish name; hasta el mediodía becomes jusqu'à midi.

forms.sourceLine: Luis: La taza cuesta 30 pesos y el vaso 35.
forms.englishPrompt: Luis: The cup costs 30 pesos and the glass 35.
forms.frenchAnswer: Luis : La tasse coûte 30 pesos et le verre 35.
forms.explanation: Cuesta maps to coûte; the unit prices 30 and 35 stay as digits, and pesos is not repeated after 35, as in the source.

forms.sourceLine: Luis: La pieza cuesta 20 pesos y la docena 200.
forms.englishPrompt: Luis: The piece costs 20 pesos and the dozen 200.
forms.frenchAnswer: Luis : La pièce coûte 20 pesos et la douzaine 200.
forms.explanation: La pièce is the unit-price term for the piece; la douzaine is the dozen; 20 and 200 stay as digits, with pesos not repeated after 200, as in the source.
Ça fait is the natural French way to check a total, parallel to ¿Son 120 pesos? The total is 2 cups at 30 plus 3 pieces at 20, which is 120.

modes.prompt: Look at the English card 'the cup' and identify its French card.
Without looking, give the French card for: the time
Partner-read: your partner reads card 14 aloud in French without showing it. Listen and give the English card. There is no recorded audio for this item.
Type the French card for 'the glass'.
Say aloud the French for: 2 americanos, please.
Write the French for: 3 pieces of sweet bread, please.
modes.targetFrench: 3 pièces de pain sucré mexicain, s'il vous plaît.

speakingObjectives: Order 2 coffees and 3 pieces of sweet bread from a barista, then repeat the total in pesos to check it.
Step 1, to the barista: 2 americanos, s'il vous plaît.
Step 2, to the barista: 3 pièces de pain sucré mexicain, s'il vous plaît.
Step 3, check the total: Ça fait 120 pesos ?
sourceNotes: The Spanish source scene is kept: Café Luna, Emma and Luis, Mexico, pesos, chilaquiles, Mexican sweet bread, and the 120-peso total (2 cups at 30 plus 3 pieces at 20).
English card faces, card kinds and Reader English lines are copied exactly from the source word list and native Reader lines.
Four source cards carry notes (the time, the piece, the serving, It's half past 8.); the French candidate carries notes on the same four cards and no others.

The source note on 'It's half past 8.' reads 'Use son las for most hours, but es la 1 for one o'clock.' French has no son las / es la split, so the note was adapted to the French point: il est for every hour, with heure or heures.
The note on 'the time' swaps ¿Qué hora es? for Quelle heure est-il ?; the note on 'the serving' swaps una orden de chilaquiles for une portion de chilaquiles; the note on 'the piece' is unchanged.
Sweet bread (pan dulce) is rendered in French as pain sucré mexicain; the Spanish loan is not used on French faces.
The first speaking objective is the source sentence verbatim; the three steps below it are French sub-steps added for this candidate.
Every mode targets a real card and carries sourceRefs to its card order (and Reader index where the line appears). The hear mode is partner-read; no recorded audio exists.
Carried over from the previous draft and not re-checked in this pass: adaptations from the private draft (euros, Lyon, fruit bowls, pastries, Café Lumière, changed prices) were not used.
residuals: The source gives 35, 200 and 45 without a currency unit; the French keeps them bare and does not add pesos.
la part was chosen over la tranche for 'the slice'; owner should confirm (see top-level residuals).
'mexicain' on card 13 and Reader line 6 is a gloss that is not in the English face.
'3 pièces de …' mirrors the source focus on la pieza and is less idiomatic than a bare count.
Model-side checks only; no human review has been performed and no audio exists.

acceptedChanges.change: Removed the false claim that the 'es la 1' note is not on the card. The source card 'It's half past 8.' does carry it; the note now states this and explains the French adaptation.

Replaced the near-tautological note with the real French point: il est for every hour, heure versus heures. Wording differs from Opus's because the note is now in English (see the adjudicator change below).
Retargeted from the non-card 'What time is it?' to card 2, 'the time' → 'l'heure'.
Added sourceRefs to every mode: see→card 5, recall→card 2, hear→card 14 and Reader 8, type→card 6, say→card 11 and Reader 4, write→card 13.
Removed the printed French from the prompt. The item is now partner-read and says outright that there is no recorded audio; audioVerified stays false.

Dropped the Spanish loan 'pan dulce' from French faces in favour of 'pain sucré mexicain', per your instruction to make the source meaning explicit. Restored 'sweet bread' in the English speaking objective.

Number spelling: digits throughout ('Il est 8 heures et demie.'). The source writes 8 as a digit, every other card uses digits, and one spelling keeps typed-answer matching simple. The forms[1] explanation no longer claims a literalness it did not have.
Replaced the stilted inversion with 'Le petit-déjeuner, c'est de 7 h à 11 h ?', which is what a customer would actually say. The added 'h' is listed in residuals.

Removed the unsourced note 'Une part de gâteau.' Kept 'la part': the only slice in the scene is a slice of cake, and 'une part de gâteau' is the standard café term, while 'tranche' suggests a flat cut of bread, ham or loaf cake. Card and Reader line 9 stay consistent.
Flagged that 'pièces' is kept for parity with the source focus on la pieza, though a bare count is more idiomatic.
The bare-number residual now lists 35, 200 and 45.
The source objective is now first and verbatim, with the barista context; the French lines follow as sub-steps, and the split is recorded in sourceNotes.
Changed to 'Les nombres, l'heure et les mesures'; the article-less version read clipped.

Card notes are now in English with French examples, mirroring the source (English notes with Spanish examples). Haiku had translated the notes into French, which a beginner cannot read. Owner should confirm this matches the convention in the other French lessons.
'2 cafés americanos' became '2 americanos'. Haiku's version put a French noun on a Spanish plural adjective; 'un americano' is the ordinary French café term and matches the English face.
Explanations now mention the unrepeated 'pesos' and spell out the 120 arithmetic. The Haiku note about the private draft is kept but marked as not re-checked.

rejectedSuggestions.suggestion: Keep the loan 'pan dulce' and add a card note glossing it.
rejectedSuggestions.reason: You asked for the explicit French meaning, and a note on card 13 would be a note the source does not have.
The candidate schema has no accepted-variants field, and the mix of words and digits would remain in a numbers lesson.

rejectedSuggestions.suggestion: Leave part versus tranche undecided for the owner, or keep the note as a flagged addition.
rejectedSuggestions.reason: You asked for a decision, so 'la part' is chosen and flagged for confirmation. The note was dropped to keep note parity with the source.

rejectedSuggestions.suggestion: Use a bare count such as '3 pains sucrés'.
rejectedSuggestions.reason: It loses the link to card 7 'la pièce' and to Reader line 7, where the piece is the pricing unit that makes the 120 total work.

rejectedSuggestions.suggestion: Keep the three-way split and only note it in sourceNotes.
rejectedSuggestions.reason: Keeping the source sentence verbatim is the stronger parity fix and restores the barista context.

residuals: Nothing here is an approval. All five gates are false, and this pass was model-side only, done without tools against the SOURCE, READER, HAIKU and OPUS text in the request; no repository files were opened.

la part versus la tranche: 'la part' is natural for cake but narrows the generic 'the slice' (rebanada). If the owner wants the generic term, change card 10 and Reader line 9 together to 'la tranche' / 'la tranche de gâteau'.

'mexicain' on card 13, Reader line 6, the write mode and speaking step 2 follows your instruction but is not in the English faces, and a customer inside a Mexican café would not normally say it. If the owner prefers strict face parity, drop it to '3 pièces de pain sucré'; card 7's note already carries the Mexican context.
'pain sucré' is a descriptive rendering, not a set French bakery category, and '3 pièces de …' is less idiomatic than a bare count. Both are kept for source parity.

'8 heures et demie' with a digit is a deliberate parity choice; French print more often uses '8 h 30' or 'huit heures et demie'. If typed answers are matched strictly, the owner may want 'huit heures et demie' accepted as a variant.
Card 16 adds 'h' ('de 7 h à 11 h'), which the source 'de 7 a 11' does not have, and uses spoken 'c'est' in place of inversion.
'americanos' and 'chilaquiles' are kept as loan words. If the owner prefers a French form for the coffee, '2 cafés américains' is the alternative.
Card notes are now in English with French examples; confirm against the note-language convention in the other French lessons.
'En tasse' on Reader line 6 mirrors 'En taza'; 'Dans une tasse' is the fuller alternative.
The sourceRefs field on modes and the partner-read wording are additions to the Haiku schema; confirm any validator or importer accepts them.
The hear mode has no recorded audio. It depends on a partner whose pronunciation is unchecked, so audioVerified must stay false.
The sourceNotes line about the private draft (euros, Lyon, Café Lumière) is carried over from Haiku and could not be checked in this pass.
